notes: Redone with live WebSearch, one search per card; each source below was in the results for that card. Search summaries only, no pages fetched. Names checked for accuracy and length (all 35 chars or fewer).

checked.found: Founded 1787 (April 12 per Philadelphia Encyclopedia; a PA marker says May 1787) by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones in Philadelphia as a mutual aid society.
Published in Boston, September 1829; Walker ran a secondhand clothing store on the Boston waterfront.
After white parents withdrew over a Black student, Crandall reopened the Canterbury, Connecticut school for Black girls in April 1833; boycott followed and the Black Law passed May 1833.
Ratified July 9, 1868; citizenship clause covers those born in the US including formerly enslaved people; equal protection clause.
Ratified February 3, 1870; bars denying the vote on account of race, effectively enfranchising Black men.
Pamphlet published October 1892 by Memphis journalist Ida B. Wells after the March 1892 Memphis lynchings; refuted the rape myth used to excuse lynching.
7 June 1893, Pietermaritzburg; a 23-year-old lawyer with a first-class ticket was forced off after a white passenger objected.
Essays and sketches published 1903 by A. C. McClurg; opens on the problem of the colour line and critiques Booker T. Washington's accommodationism.
UNIA founded in Kingston, Jamaica, July/August 1914 (sources vary on day); later grew in the US from 1916.
Year 1919 is correct (Paris, 19-21 February 1919, timed with the peace conference). The description's 'post-war' is a dating word that implies the era.
checked.suggestion: Black leaders from Africa, the Caribbean and America met alongside a major peace conference in Paris to press for equality and colonial reform.

checked.found: Organised 25 August 1925 in Harlem under A. Philip Randolph; first Black-led union chartered by the AFL (1935).
Signed June 25, 1941 after Randolph's threatened July 1 march; banned discrimination in defense industries.
Executive Order 9981 signed July 26, 1948, abolishing segregation in the armed forces (implementation gradual).
Reagan signed the King holiday bill on November 2, 1983 (a few sources say Nov 3).
1984 Nobel Peace Prize to Desmond Tutu for non-violent campaign against apartheid; ceremony 10 December 1984.
